mainTopic: Reading the weekly פרשה with the ציבור, advice from רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבא, and the deadline for the night שמע
overview: The גמרא finishes the rule that a person should read each weekly פרשה twice in the original and once in תרגום, together with the ציבור, even verses that are only lists of place names. Then comes a story: רב ביבי בר אביי learns that ערב יום כיפור is a day for eating, not for catching up, and that he may not read ahead early either. רבי יהושע בן לוי gives his sons three pieces of advice: finish your portions with the ציבור, cut the ורידין when slaughtering, and keep honoring a זקן who forgot his learning. רבא also gives his sons advice: don't cut meat on your hand, don't sit on the bed of an ארמית, and don't pass behind a בית הכנסת during davening. אביי then limits that last rule. רבי עקיבא and רבן גמליאל praise good habits of the מדיים and the פרסיים. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and rules like רבן גמליאל: the night שמע may be read until dawn. It brings two ברייתות of רבי שמעון בן יוחי about reading שמע twice, once around dawn and once around sunrise, and finds a contradiction in each. The first contradiction is answered on this amud, and the answer to the second comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a verse of place names must be read, and the reward is long life
steps.stepSummary: The rule of reading the פרשה twice plus תרגום once applies even to a verse that is only a list of names. Whoever finishes his portions with the ציבור gets a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies even to the verse 'Atarot and Divon.' Anyone who finishes his portions along with the congregation is given long days and years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the rule it already started: read each weekly פרשה twice and its תרגום once. It adds that this includes even a verse of plain place names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'עטרות ודיבן' is just a list of towns, so you might think there is nothing to translate or repeat. The גמרא says you still read it fully, with no shortcuts. The reward for keeping pace with the ציבור is a long life.

keyTerms.meaning: together with the congregation, keeping their schedule
his days are lengthened (he gets long life)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the practice of שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום, done in step with the weekly קריאת התורה.

phrases.english: And even 'Atarot and Divon.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 32:3. That verse is just a list of towns, and it still has to be read twice and translated once.

phrases.english: For anyone who completes his portions with the congregation
has his days and his years lengthened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the teaching from the previous section about completing the פרשיות with the ציבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every verse must be read twice plus once in תרגום, even lists of names. Completing the portions with the ציבור brings long life.

steps.title: רב ביבי's plan to catch up on ערב יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי planned to make up all the year's missed portions on ערב יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי thought to finish all the portions of the whole year on ערב יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: A story starts here. רב ביבי had fallen behind and planned to catch up on everything on ערב יום כיפור. This sets up the next move, where someone pushes back on his plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He clearly took the obligation seriously, since he wanted to make up every portion. The question is only when. ערב יום כיפור seemed like a free day before the holy day.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום כיפור, the day before יום כיפור

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye thought
to complete the portions of the whole year
on the eve of Yom Kippur,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי סָבַר לְאַשְׁלוֹמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the duty from step 1 to a real case of someone who fell behind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי's proposal: make up all missed portions on ערב יום כיפור.

steps.title: חייא בר רב מדפתי quotes a פסוק against the plan
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב מדפתי quoted the פסוק saying 'you shall afflict yourselves on the ninth of the month in the evening.'
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב מדפתי taught him: It is written, 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth of the month in the evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רב ביבי's plan by quoting a פסוק about יום כיפור that mentions the ninth day. The next steps explain why that פסוק matters here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ninth of תשרי is ערב יום כיפור itself. By quoting this פסוק, חייא hints that the ninth day has its own special job, so it should not be used for catching up on reading.

keyTerms.meaning: he taught him, quoting a source
and you shall afflict your souls (fast)
on the ninth of the month

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי:
phrases.english: Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti taught him:
It is written: 'And you shall afflict your souls
on the ninth of the month in the evening.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רב ביבי's plan from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to spend ערב יום כיפור catching up on the portions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah gives the ninth day its own meaning, which step 5 explains, so it should not be taken up with making up reading.

steps.title: But the fast is on the tenth, not the ninth
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'the ninth,' yet the fast is on the tenth. Why does the Torah say the ninth?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we fast on the ninth? We fast on the tenth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the wording of the פסוק. It sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just a few verses earlier, the Torah says יום כיפור is the tenth of תשרי. So mentioning 'the ninth' must be teaching something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: but is it so? (a question of surprise)
but surely; isn't it so that...

phrases.english: But do we fast on the ninth?!
Don't we fast on the tenth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק link the affliction to the ninth when the fast is on the tenth?

steps.title: Eating on the ninth counts like fasting
steps.stepSummary: Whoever eats and drinks on the ninth is credited as if he fasted on both the ninth and the tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to tell you: anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth, the verse counts it for him as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Mentioning the ninth teaches that eating on ערב יום כיפור is a מצוה, worth as much as a fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating on the ninth gets the same credit as fasting. So ערב יום כיפור is meant for eating and drinking. That is why רב ביבי should not fill the day with catching up on the portions.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, it comes to tell you

steps.whatToRemember: Eating and drinking on ערב יום כיפור is a מצוה. It counts as if one fasted two days, so the day is not set aside for catching up on Torah reading.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mean we fast on the ninth. The fast is on the tenth. The 'ninth' teaches the value of eating the day before.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the מצוה of eating on ערב יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you
anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth,
the verse counts it for him
as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4, and that answer is the reason behind the challenge in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'ninth' teaches that eating on ערב יום כיפור is credited like fasting, so the day belongs to eating, not to catching up on reading.

steps.title: רב ביבי's new plan: read ahead early
steps.stepSummary: Since ערב יום כיפור was ruled out, רב ביבי thought to read the portions ahead of time instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then thought to read them early.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי suggests a new idea: read the portions before the ציבור reaches them. This sets up the elder's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you cannot catch up late in one burst, maybe you can stay ahead by reading early. This is a new way of meeting the same obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: to do them early, ahead of time

phrases.english: He thought to read them early,
phrases.notes: This is still רב ביבי. Now he wants to read ahead of the ציבור instead of catching up later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the plan in step 2 was rejected, he offers another approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposal: read the portions before the ציבור does.

steps.title: An elder rules: not early and not late
steps.stepSummary: An elder quoted a teaching: one may not read early or late. It must be together with the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: We learned, 'As long as he does not read early and does not read late.'
steps.whatsHappening: An unnamed elder rejects the plan to read early by quoting a learned teaching. The portions must be read in step with the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words from step 1 were 'עם הציבור,' together with the congregation. Reading early breaks that just as much as reading late does. So both of רב ביבי's ideas are ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: as long as; on condition that
do it early / do it late

steps.whatToRemember: Read the weekly פרשה together with the ציבור: not early and not late.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him,
We learned: as long as he does not read early
and does not read late.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative plan from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out reading the portions ahead of the ציבור, and repeats that reading late is also wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The obligation is to read together with the ציבור, so reading early breaks it just as reading late does.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The portions must be read at the same time as the ציבור, neither ahead nor behind.

steps.title: Finish your portions together with the community
steps.stepSummary: The elder's rule from Step 7 (read with the ציבור) is backed up by רבי יהושע בן לוי's instruction to his sons to finish their portions with the ציבור: the text twice and the תרגום once.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי told his sons: Complete your weekly Torah portions together with the community, reading the text twice and the Aramaic translation once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for what the elder told רב ביבי: the weekly portion should be read in step with the ציבור. It quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי, who gave his sons this same advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the elder said you may not read ahead or fall behind. Here רבי יהושע בן לוי's words 'with the community' confirm that the timing matters, not just the reading. He also spells out the method: the text twice and the תרגום once.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with the community, on the same schedule
Reading the Torah text twice and the Aramaic translation once

steps.whatToRemember: The weekly portion is reviewed in step with the ציבור, not early and not late: the text twice and the תרגום once.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the practice of reviewing each week's פרשה as 'שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום'.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said to his sons:
Complete your portions with the community,
the text twice and the translation once.
phrases.notes: 'תרגום' here means the Aramaic translation of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the elder's rejection (Step 7) of רב ביבי's plan to read early.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must read the portion together with the ציבור, not early or late.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's instruction to his sons: 'אשלימו פרשיותייכו עם הציבור'.

steps.title: Be careful to cut the jugular veins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי also told his sons to be careful to cut the ורידין when slaughtering, following רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And be careful with the jugular veins, following רבי יהודה, as we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, the slaughter is not finished until he cuts the veins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues listing רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to his sons. This piece is about שחיטה: make sure to cut the jugular veins too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי backs his advice with a משנה where רבי יהודה says the slaughter needs the ורידין to be cut. By telling his sons to 'be careful' to act like רבי יהודה, he is giving them a practice to follow, presented as extra care.

keyTerms.meaning: The jugular veins in the neck
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: And be careful with the jugular veins, like Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
until he slaughters the jugular veins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second piece of רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to his sons. It moves from Torah reading to שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When slaughtering, be careful to cut the ורידין as well, as רבי יהודה says.

steps.title: Respect an elder who forgot his learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי's third piece of advice: keep honoring a זקן who forgot his Torah through no fault of his own, just as the broken לוחות were kept in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And be careful to respect an elder who forgot his learning because of circumstances beyond his control. As we say: both the tablets and the broken tablets were placed in the Ark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third piece of רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice: don't stop respecting a Torah scholar who lost his learning because of illness or hardship. It backs this up with the broken לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broken first לוחות were not thrown away. They were kept in the ארון next to the whole ones. In the same way, a scholar who forgot his Torah, like broken לוחות, still deserves honor for the Torah he once held.

keyTerms.meaning: The broken pieces of the first tablets

steps.whatToRemember: A scholar who forgot his Torah through no fault of his own is still honored, like the broken לוחות that stayed in the ארון.

phrases.english: And be careful with an elder
who forgot his learning because of circumstances beyond his control.
As we say: the tablets and the broken tablets
are placed in the Ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִזָּהֲרוּ בְּזָקֵן שֶׁשָּׁכַח תַּלְמוּדוֹ מֵחֲמַת אוֹנְסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third piece of רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice, in the same 'והזהרו' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must keep honoring a זקן who forgot his learning through no fault of his own, as shown by the broken לוחות kept in the ארון.

steps.title: רבא's advice: don't cut meat on your hand
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his sons not to cut meat while holding it on their hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to his sons: When you cut meat, don't cut it on your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new set of advice, this time from רבא to his sons. The first piece is practical: don't cut meat while holding it on your hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like רבי יהושע בן לוי, רבא gives his sons guidance for daily life. The rule is stated here, and the גמרא will explain the reason in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said to his sons:
When you cut meat,
do not cut it on your hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new list of advice, from רבא this time instead of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not cut meat while holding it on your hand.

steps.title: Two reasons for not cutting on your hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two explanations for רבא's advice: because of danger, or because it could ruin the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: because of danger. And some say: because it could ruin the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא said not to cut meat on your hand. It brings two different opinions about the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says the worry is danger: you might cut yourself. The other view says the worry is the meal: even a small cut could get blood on the meat and spoil it. Both views agree with the rule and only disagree about the reason.

phrases.english: Some say: because of danger.
And some say: because of ruining the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבא's rule in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question left unasked: why not cut meat on your hand?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either because of danger of cutting yourself, or because it might ruin the meal.

steps.title: Two more pieces of advice from רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his sons not to sit on the bed of an ארמית, and not to pass behind a בית הכנסת while the ציבור is davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman, and do not pass behind the synagogue while the congregation is praying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues the list of advice to his sons that began in Step 11, adding two more rules. The גמרא will explain each one in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are short, unexplained instructions. The first, about the bed of an ארמית, is unclear and the גמרא will offer three readings of it. The second, about passing behind a בית הכנסת, will be tied to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The bed of an Aramean woman, meaning a non-Jewish woman

phrases.english: And do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman,
and do not pass behind the synagogue
at the time when the congregation is praying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list of advice after the explanation in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not sit on the bed of an ארמית, and do not pass behind a בית הכנסת while the ציבור is davening.

steps.title: Three ways to understand the bed of an Aramean woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three readings: don't sleep without קריאת שמע, don't marry a גיורת, or literally don't sit on a non-Jewish woman's bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it means: do not go to sleep without saying קריאת שמע. Others say: do not marry a woman who converted. And others say: it means an actual Aramean woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבא's first rule again and explains what it means. It brings three different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two readings take the words as a picture for something else: sleeping without קריאת שמע is like sleeping like a non-Jew, and marrying a גיורת is marrying someone from a non-Jewish background. The third reading takes the words at face value, and the next step backs it up with a story.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; introduces one of several opinions

phrases.english: And 'do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman' —
some say
do not go to sleep without reciting Shema,
and some say
that you should not marry a woman who converted.
And some say:
an actual Aramean woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לָא תִּגְנוֹ בְּלָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of the first rule from Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'do not sit on the bed of an ארמית' mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three readings: don't sleep without קריאת שמע; don't marry a גיורת; literally a non-Jewish woman's bed.

steps.title: The story of רב פפא and the bed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא refused to sit on an ארמית's bed until she lifted it, and a dead baby was found; from this the חכמים forbade sitting on such a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because of what happened to רב פפא. He went to an Aramean woman, and she brought out a bed and told him to sit. He said he would not sit until she lifted the bed. She lifted it, and they found a dead baby there. From this the Sages said: it is forbidden to sit on the bed of an Aramean woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that explains where the literal reading (the third opinion) comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The literal reading is not just a guess. It is based on a real event: had רב פפא sat down, he could have been blamed for the baby's death. That is why the חכמים made a rule against sitting on such a bed.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: And this is because of an incident with Rav Pappa.
For Rav Pappa went to an Aramean woman,
and she brought out a bed for him.
She said to him: Sit!
He said to her: I will not sit
until you lift up the bed.
She lifted the bed
and they found a dead baby there.
From here the Sages said:
It is forbidden to sit on the bed of an Aramean woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the literal reading, the third opinion in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The literal reading: do not sit on a non-Jewish woman's bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident with רב פפא, where a dead baby was found under the bed.

steps.title: רבא's advice matches רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule about not passing behind a בית הכנסת during davening supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not pass behind the synagogue while the congregation is praying' supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: a person is forbidden to pass behind the synagogue while the congregation is praying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבא's second rule and points out that it backs up a ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different אמוראים say the same rule, so each strengthens the other. The worry is that people who see him walk past will think he is avoiding davening with the ציבור.

phrases.english: And 'do not pass behind the synagogue
while the congregation is praying' —

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: this supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A person is forbidden to pass
behind the synagogue
while the congregation is praying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the second rule from Step 13 and links it to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule against passing behind a בית הכנסת during davening.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's advice to his sons, which says the same thing.

steps.title: אביי limits when the rule applies
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the rule applies only if there is no other door, no other בית הכנסת, and the person is not carrying a load, running, or wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this when there is no other entrance; if there is another entrance, there is no problem. And only when there is no other synagogue; if there is, there is no problem. And only when he is not carrying a load, not running, and not wearing תפילין; if any one of these applies, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds three limits to רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule, showing when it does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule exists because onlookers might think he is skipping davening. If there is another door or another בית הכנסת, they can assume he is going there. If he is carrying a load or running, he is clearly busy, and if he wears תפילין, people see he is God-fearing, so no one will suspect him.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when; introduces a limit on a rule
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: Passing behind a בית הכנסת during davening is forbidden only when people might think you are avoiding davening. If there is another door, another בית הכנסת, or a clear sign of why you are passing (a load, running, תפילין), it is allowed.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: We only said this where there is no other entrance,
but if there is another entrance —
we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: And we only said this where there is no other synagogue,
but if there is another synagogue —
we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא דָּרֵי טוּנָא,
phrases.english: And we only said this where he is not carrying a load,
and not running, and not wearing tefillin,
but if one of these applies —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי quoted in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule applies only if there is no other door, no other בית הכנסת, and he is not carrying a load, running, or wearing תפילין.

steps.title: Three good habits of the Medes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא praising the מדיים for three habits: cutting meat only on a table, kissing only the back of the hand, and taking counsel only in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא said, "I like the מדיים for three things. When they cut meat, they cut it only on a table. When they kiss, they kiss only the back of the hand. When they take counsel, they do it only in a field."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא lists three good habits of the מדיים that are worth learning from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of good conduct from רבא's advice to his sons. It also fits with רבא's warning not to cut meat on one's hand, since the מדיים cut meat only on a table. Each habit shows care: safe and clean eating, respectful affection, and keeping private plans private.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
They take counsel, make plans together

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַמָּדִיִּים,
phrases.english: For three things I like the Medes:
When they cut meat,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹתְכִין אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי הַשּׁוּלְחָן,
phrases.english: they cut it only on top of the table;

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁנּוֹשְׁקִין — אֵין נוֹשְׁקִין אֶלָּא עַל גַּב הַיָּד,
phrases.english: when they kiss, they kiss only on the back of the hand;
and when they take counsel, they take counsel only in the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of good conduct from רבא's advice, now using praiseworthy habits of another nation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three habits of the מדיים are worth copying: cut meat on a table, kiss the back of the hand, and take counsel in a field.

steps.title: A verse for taking counsel in the field
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה brings a פסוק showing that יעקב called רחל and לאה out to the field to talk privately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: What is the source for this? "And יעקב sent and called רחל and לאה to the field, to his flock."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה finds a source in the תורה for the third habit, taking counsel only in a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יעקב needed to discuss running away from לבן, he did not talk at home. He called his wives out to the field, where no one could overhear. This shows the habit of the מדיים is supported by the behavior of יעקב אבינו.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (the source in the פסוקים)
Field, an open place where no one can overhear

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
What is the verse for this?
"And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah
to the field, to his flock."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק supporting the third habit in רבי עקיבא's list.
steps.raayaObject: The habit of taking counsel only in a field
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 31:4, where יעקב calls רחל and לאה to the field

steps.title: Three modest habits of the Persians
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן גמליאל praising the פרסיים for being modest in eating, in the bathroom, and in marital matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבן גמליאל said, "I like the פרסיים for three things. They are modest in their eating, modest in the bathroom, and modest in 'another matter.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא, this time from רבן גמליאל, listing three things he likes about the פרסיים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as רבי עקיבא's list, with "three things I like" about a nation. Here all three habits are about צניעות, being private and dignified in personal matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "another thing"; a polite way to refer to marital relations

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Gamliel said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַפַּרְסִיִּים:
phrases.english: For three things I like the Persians:
they are modest in their eating,
and modest in the bathroom,
and modest in another matter.
phrases.notes: "Another matter" is the polite way of saying marital relations, without naming it outright.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list to רבי עקיבא's, praising a different nation for different habits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרסיים are praised for modesty in eating, in the bathroom, and in marital relations.

steps.title: The Persians are destined for punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads a פסוק in ישעיהו as describing the פרסיים, sent as tools of ה׳'s anger, as "set aside" for גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: "I have commanded My consecrated ones." רב יוסף taught: These are the פרסיים, who are "consecrated" and set aside for גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after praising the פרסיים, the גמרא brings רב יוסף's teaching that the פרסיים are destined for גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מקודשי usually sounds like "holy ones," but רב יוסף reads it as "designated" or "set aside." The פרסיים were sent to carry out ה׳'s anger against בבל, and they are set aside for גיהנם. So good manners in a few areas do not erase the overall verdict on this nation.

keyTerms.meaning: My consecrated ones; here read as "those set aside"
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.confusionAlert: Here מקודשין does not mean holy. It means set aside or designated, in this case for punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא praises specific habits of the מדיים and פרסיים that are worth learning from, but praising a habit is not praising the whole nation. רב יוסף still says the פרסיים are destined for גיהנם.

phrases.english: "I have commanded My consecrated ones"
Rav Yosef taught:
These are the Persians, who are consecrated
and designated for Gehenna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי צִוֵּיתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁי, תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Balances רבן גמליאל's praise of the פרסיים with a harsh overall verdict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרסיים in ישעיהו 13:3 are "consecrated" in the sense of being designated for גיהנם.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: After the side discussions, the גמרא returns to the משנה and rules like רבן גמליאל, who says the night שמע may be read until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the משנה, where רבן גמליאל said you may read שמע until dawn. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the halacha follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and gives a final ruling: we follow רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים set a deadline of midnight for the evening שמע, and רבן גמליאל said until dawn. שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל, so the evening שמע can be read all night long, until dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, the first light of morning
"Etc.": a short way of quoting the rest of the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line: the evening שמע may be read until dawn, as רבן גמליאל says.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says, etc.:
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, where רבן גמליאל said you may read שמע until dawn.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the מדיים and the פרסיים and goes back to the משנה's argument about the deadline for the evening שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבן גמליאל: the evening שמע may be read until dawn.

steps.title: Reading שמע twice, just before and just after dawn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי says a person can read שמע just before dawn and again just after dawn, and count one as the night reading and one as the day reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says that sometimes a person reads שמע twice at night, once before dawn and once after dawn. With these two readings he covers both obligations, one for the day and one for the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses רבן גמליאל's 'until dawn' rule. Someone can read the night שמע just before dawn and the morning שמע right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the night שמע is good until dawn, the reading just before dawn counts for the night. The reading just after dawn counts for the day. So two readings only minutes apart can cover both obligations.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was taught": opens a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
His obligation (to be יוצא is to fulfill it)

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says
Sometimes a person reads Shema
twice at night,
once before dawn comes up
and once after dawn comes up,
and with them he fulfills his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל יוֹם וְאַחַת שֶׁל לַיְלָה.
phrases.english: one of the day and one of the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical result of רבן גמליאל's 'until dawn' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading שמע just before dawn and again just after dawn covers both the night and the day obligations.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא calls the time after dawn 'night' but also says the reading then counts for 'day'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא contradicts itself. First you said a person reads שמע twice 'at night', which means the time after dawn is still night. Then you taught that one reading counts for the day, which means that time is day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the inside. The beginning and the end seem to disagree about whether the time just after dawn is night or day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'twice at night' put both readings, including the one after dawn, at night. But 'one of the day' says the reading after dawn counts as the morning שמע, which needs to be read in the day. One time cannot be both.

keyTerms.meaning: "This itself is difficult": the source contradicts itself
"Apparently" / "so we see": draws a conclusion from wording

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against רבן גמליאל or the halacha. It only asks how one ברייתא can call the same moment both night and day.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
phrases.english: you said: sometimes a person reads Shema
twice at night,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא לְאַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר לֵילְיָא הוּא,
phrases.english: so apparently after dawn comes up it is night,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
phrases.english: and then it teaches: with them he fulfills his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל יוֹם וְאַחַת שֶׁל לַיְלָה,
phrases.english: one of the day and one of the night,
so apparently it is day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא brought in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening of the ברייתא treats the time after dawn as night, while the ending treats it as day. That is an internal contradiction.

steps.title: It is really night, but people are already getting up
steps.stepSummary: The time just after dawn really is night. The ברייתא calls it 'day' because some people already get up then, so a reading at that time counts as the morning שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, there is no contradiction. The time after dawn really is night. The ברייתא calls it 'day' only because there are people who get up at that hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The time after dawn is truly night, and it is called 'day' for a narrow reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first wording, 'at night', is the precise one. The word 'day' does not mean it is daytime. It means that hour already counts as the time people get up, so the morning שמע can be read then.

keyTerms.meaning: "Really" / "actually": holds on to one side of the question

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל: the night שמע may be read until dawn. The time just after dawn is still night, but because some people are already up, a reading then can count as the morning שמע.

phrases.english: No, it really is night.
And the fact that it calls it "day"
is because there are people
who get up at that hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the wording: one word is taken literally ('night') and the other is given a looser meaning ('day').
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to call the time after dawn both night and day.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is truly night. It is called 'day' only because some people get up then, so the morning שמע can be read at that time.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר חנינא, quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי, rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי's ברייתא about reading שמע twice around dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a ruling: we follow רבי שמעון בן יוחי. In practice, one reading just before dawn and one just after can count as the night שמע and the day שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling refers to the ברייתא from step 23, which was explained in steps 24-25. The time just after dawn really is night, but it can also count for the morning שמע. Now an אמורא tells us this is the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports the ruling
The earlier אמורא in whose name the ruling is said

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns רבי שמעון בן יוחי's ברייתא from an opinion into practical הלכה.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ḥanina said,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 23, about reading just before and just after dawn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא just explained in steps 23-25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי: two readings around dawn can count as the night שמע and the day שמע.

steps.title: Another version places the ruling on a different ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב אחא בר חנינא's ruling was said about another ברייתא, where רבי שמעון בן יוחי quotes רבי עקיבא: reading once before sunrise and once after counts as the night and day readings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach רב אחא בר חנינא's ruling on a different source. In that ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן יוחי says in the name of רבי עקיבא: sometimes a person reads שמע twice in the day, once before sunrise and once after, and this covers both obligations, one for day and one for night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second version: the same ruling was really attached to a similar ברייתא. That ברייתא talks about sunrise, הנץ החמה, instead of dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות have the same idea: two readings close together around daybreak cover both the night and day obligations. The difference is the time marker. The first spoke of dawn (עמוד השחר), and this one speaks of sunrise (הנץ החמה). This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will find a contradiction inside this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (another version of who said what, or about what)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ברייתות. The first (step 23) is about dawn, עמוד השחר. This one is about sunrise, הנץ החמה, which comes later.

phrases.english: There are those who teach

phrases.aramaic: לְהָא דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אַהָא.
phrases.english: this statement of Rav Aḥa bar Ḥanina about this one:
phrases.notes: In other words, the same ruling was said about the next ברייתא instead of the earlier one.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
Sometimes a person reads the Shema
twice in the day,
once before sunrise,
and once after sunrise,
and he fulfills his obligation with them,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל יוֹם וְאַחַת שֶׁל לַיְלָה.
phrases.english: one for the day and one for the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of which ברייתא the ruling in step 26 was said about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the ruling follows רבי שמעון בן יוחי quoting רבי עקיבא: readings just before and just after sunrise cover both the night and day obligations.

steps.title: The sunrise ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא calls both readings 'in the day', which makes the time before sunrise day. But it also says one reading counts for night, which makes that same time night.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is hard on its own terms. You said a person reads שמע twice 'in the day', so the time before sunrise must be daytime. Then you taught that one reading counts for the day and one for the night, so that time must be night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the inside. Two of its phrases seem to give opposite answers about the time before sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'twice in the day' suggest that both readings, including the one before sunrise, happen during the day. But 'one for the night' needs the before-sunrise reading to be at night, or it couldn't count as the night שמע. So the same time seems to be called both day and night, which sets up an answer to come.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (the source contradicts itself)

phrases.english: This itself is difficult.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
phrases.english: You said: Sometimes a person reads the Shema
twice in the day,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קוֹדֶם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה יְמָמָא הוּא,
phrases.english: evidently, before sunrise is daytime;
and then it teaches:
he fulfills his obligation with them,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל יוֹם וְאַחַת שֶׁל לַיְלָה,
phrases.english: one for the day and one for the night;
evidently, it is night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא just quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי quoting רבי עקיבא about sunrise
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Twice in the day' makes the time before sunrise day, while 'one for the night' makes that same time night. The ברייתא seems to say both.
